correctness.rationale: For all finite nontrivial 2-(v,k,1) designs, NN^T=(r-1)I+J gives v>=k(k-1)+1. Complete extension inventory for every ordered triple including repetitions: collinear triples admit k-3 fresh points on their line and v-k off; noncollinear triples admit k-2 points on each of three distinct pair-lines and v-3k+3 >= (k-2)^2 generic points. These positive/nonpositive statuses depend only on k=3 versus k>=4. Backward four-round EF induction proves equivalence within each part; existence of four distinct collinear points separates parts at rank four, and rank-three game equivalence gives sharpness. Programmatic checks on five valid designs independently agree but do not replace the all-design proof.

originality.rationale: No examined archived/result-indexed statement implies the same two rank-four equivalence classes for every finite nontrivial Steiner 2-design in the points-only ternary collinearity signature. value.rationale: This is a complete natural finite-model-theoretic classification across every nontrivial Steiner 2-design, allowing arbitrary block size and nonisomorphic designs. It identifies the first observable point-collinearity resource (four nested quantifiers) and demonstrates that all higher block sizes are invisible at that resource level, despite huge geometric variation. The Fisher reservoir plus full extension inventory is a structural argument, not a numerical slice or merely a known-table calculation. The exact two-class quotient is intrinsically meaningful in comparing the expressive power of point-only versus incidence languages.
